front.text:
The brutish man charges at you with single-minded fury, but you haven't found the missing ship just to cut and run now. His talents prove no match for yours, and within a minute, the man lies on his back on the ship's deck, groaning and clutching his head with both hands. With witnesses hard to come by, you demand that the man tell everything he knows. The man thrashes for a moment, and his eyes snap open with a roar. "The dreamer stirs! In stone it lies dead, with stone shall it awaken!" He spews a series of words that you can't even begin to identify until finally his eyes roll backward and he drops back unconscious, twitching lightly. Is this man possessed? A fanatic? Both? You can only assume that he is a sailor based on his tattoos and clothing, but he is clearly more than that. His work on the ship served some darker power, willing or otherwise.
Add this card to the victory display and remember that you "subdued the attacker."
Victory 1.

front.flavor_text: Whether the ship has been hidden or sunk, you won't get any concrete answers about the missing cargo until you can confirm the location of the Myra Louise.  A towboat of its size must still be on the river somewhere, and hopefully some witnesses along the Miskatonic's banks can point you in the right direction.

back.name: Up the River
back.text:
There's no shortage of palms waiting to be greased, but you manage to weed out the irrelevant information from the parts that actually point you in the right direction. Several sailors saw the Myra Louise sail into Arkham last night, but it sailed straight through Arkham further upriver without making any stops.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Reveal each Arkham location, then remove all clues from each location in play. Put the set-aside Main Deck, Wheelhouse, and Engine Room locations into play. Remove the Unfriendly Ports encounter set from the game. Shuffle the encounter deck if it was searched. This set is indicated by the following icon:

front.text: <obj> If an investigator enters the Main Deck, advance.
front.flavor_text: You trek up the banks of the river west out of town.  It doesn't take long before you spot the ship on a small offshoot of the river, anchored in the darkness of nearby trees.  While silent, the ship is not uninhabited, and you can spot a lone figure moving slowly and deliberately about the main deck.

back.name: Dark Deeds at Work
back.text:
You move cautiously up the gangplank to the Myra Louise's deck and peer over the railing. On the opposite side, a towering man hoists a body in an expensive suit and hurls it over the side of the ship. You crane your head up to get a good look at the body, but it's just enough for the man to spot you as he turns back toward the ship. "Who the hell're you?!" he bellows, advancing toward you with powerful strides.
Spawn the set-aside Bill Bledsoe at the Main Deck.

front.flavor_text: You've found the Myra Louise, and a fresh set of trouble to go with it.  The presence of the brutish man and the well-dressed corpse already compounds the mystery, but there's sure to be even more evidence somewhere on the ship.  Whatever you choose to pursue, you'll have to work quickly while you can still endure the constant attacks, terrible weather, and strange influence you feel at the back of your brain.

back.name: Only Just Begun
back.text:
Your search of the Myra Louise has provided some very strange insights, but there's no sign of the actual cargo you were hired to find. You decide to retreat with the information you've gathered to figure out where to try next.
(R3)

front.flavor_text: By the time you arrive at the riverfront, the storm has grown to a steady drizzle.  Rain pelts the tin roofs and buffets the already cascading waves, some reaching high enough to wash over the docks.  The worst of the storm has yet to make landfall.

back.name: Sheets of Rain
back.text:
A sudden surge in wind brings the approaching storm in force. Rain plasters you all at once, and the gale nearly pushes you off balance. You brace yourself against the storm and push on, determined not to let the weather end your investigation early.
Search the encounter deck and discard pile for a copy of Driving Rain and put it into play. Shuffle the encounter deck if it was searched.

front.flavor_text: Amid the downpour sweeping through Arkham, the Miskatonic river grows steadily wilder.  A faint saltwater smell lingers on the air as you soldier on, but what could bring such a smell to an inland town on a freshwater river?

back.name: Webbed Hands and      Razor Teeth
back.text:
From out of the water rises a grotesque figure, skin shining from any nearby lights. Its posture and rapid approach clearly show the creature's intentions of attacking you. You scramble to defend yourself against this added menace.
Search the encounter deck and discard pile for a Deep Oneor Hybridenemy and spawn it at the lead investigator's location (2 enemies instead if there are 3 or 4 investigators in the game). Shuffle the encounter deck if it was searched.

front.flavor_text: The rain keeps pounding and the fishlike creatures rise from and sink back into the river, but your challenges are far from over.  The faint feeling at the back of your mind spikes up strongly, a distant influence that gnaws at your very core.

back.name: Flashes of Nightmare
back.text:
Your endurance finally peaks between the fearsome attackers, battering weather, and waves of pain inside your mind. You collapse down in agony, unable to keep up your search any longer.
Each investigator is defeated and takes 1 physical or mental trauma (your choice).

front.text:
After a few tense minutes of reassurance, you manage to calm the stoker, but you find some difficulty in speaking with him. His thick accent and broken grammar show that he hasn't been in America for very long. The man collapses to his seat and rubs his forehead with tearful relief. "You are... save me from them. Men with guns. They say to stand at corner. Not let us talk. I hear sound of them take cargo." The stoker licks his dry lips as he tries to focus his memories. "Boat stop and we wait long time. Then... air turn... waves. Strange sight and sound. Then... monsters come. Fight men with guns. I hide in coal, but... friends not fast." He looks to the bodies of his former crewmates and makes the sign of the cross. You comfort the man and assure him of his safety while making a mental note of what happened to the ship's cargo.
Add this card to the victory display and remember that you "talked to a survivor."
Victory 1.

back.name: Someone Else's Problem
back.text:
As you mingle with the other socialites and criminals, it quickly becomes apparent that the auction has a lot going on beneath the surface. Mixed into the crowds are several dark figures that keep trying to corner and eliminate you, and you're not even sure if they're with the O'Bannions or not. However, between the action, you are able to observe yet another out-of-place figure. Tips from other patrons help you to identify a member of the Sheldon Gang – one of the O'Bannions' rivals – casing the auction house. You pass this tip to the O'Bannion sentries, who advance into the crowd, leaving you free access to the back rooms. Duty is one thing, but bad blood is another.
Reveal Service Corridor and put the set-aside Storage Vault location into play.

front.text: <obj> If Storage Vault is revealed and there are no clues on it, advance.
front.flavor_text: You've got to make the most of your time before the O'Bannions tighten their security once more.  If the stolen artifacts are anywhere on the premises, then there's only one place to look.

back.name: The Warped Idol
back.text:
Your search through the auction storage grows steadily more frustrating. Actual tons of artifacts are nowhere to be found, and you keep grappling with some strange force that threatens to eject you from the storage room entirely. As you move to lift another crate, a small bundle slides off and drops to the ground. Your eye catches the word "Mycenae" stamped across the paper, and you immediately seize and unwrap it. Beneath the waxed paper is a curious stone object, about the size of a bottle, carved into an unrecognizable shape. The figurine proves difficult to hold, as its contours do not match up to what you see before you. You don't have much time to examine the object before the sound of echoing footsteps brings you back to the present. There will be time for study later, and there are more unanswered questions to consider.
Choose an investigator to take control of the set-aside Warped Idol. For the remainder of the scenario, this asset does not take up any slots. Add a token to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Spawn the set-aside O'Bannion Sentry at Service Corridor. Put the set-aside Broker's Office into play.

front.text: <obj> If each undefeated investigator has resigned, advance.
front.flavor_text: The bizarre idol is proof enough of the O'Bannions' theft of the cargo, but the rest of the artifacts have vanished, and you still don't know why the gangsters hijacked the shipment in the first place.  You may be able to find answers with the auction broker who handles all the transactions, but you must also consider your safe retreat with the idol in hand.

back.name: Close the Deal
back.text:
If there are at least 1 clues on Nora Shanley:
After minutes of pleading and badgering, the woman lets out an exasperated exhale of smoke. "Alright, alright, fine. I've seen a lot of stupid people mess with the O'Bannions before, but this has got to take the cake. I want to hear your reason for all this, and it had better be a good one."
(R2) Otherwise:
You make for the exits as discreetly as possible, but the O'Bannions catch sight of you leaving the backroom on your way out. The gangsters look far angrier than you expected, and a bit worn out, giving you a small advantage in the race for the front door.
(R1)

front.flavor_text: Now inside the auction house, your task truly begins.  The O'Bannions are watching the crowds carefully, so you'll have to maintain an alibi.  Bidding on some of the items up for auction should convince them.

back.name: One Final Bid
back.text: "Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes tonight's auction." The auctioneer bangs his gavel a final time before stepping down from the lectern, the abruptness leaving the bidders in a slight uproar. The O'Bannions rush through the final transactions and herd the rest toward the exits. With no further business, your presence here will only be tolerated a short while longer.

front.flavor_text: With the auction concluded, you have a brief window before your status as a guest is reduced to trespasser.  You don't want to test the O'Bannions' capacity as hosts any more than you have to.

back.name: Past Due
back.text:
Before you can make your exit, a half dozen gangsters corner you with sadistic smirks on their faces. Several of them tighten their grip around blunt instruments as the leader of the pack speaks. "You know what's coming, but I'm a fair man. I'll even give you a head start. You have until the end of this sentence."
Each investigator who has not resigned is defeated and takes a physical trauma as the O'Bannions "escort" them from the premises.

Wycliffe's papers transition suddenly to a strange code.
Where have you seen this writing before?

front.text:
The final member of the strange group collapses against a wall and slides down to the ground, dead. You catch your breath and scan the darkened corners of the room for more before you calm yourself and begin to search the bodies. On one of the men, you find an opened letter, written on stationery from Wycliffe's own desk, and in his hand. You can only guess whether this letter was sent to the agents' employer or just intercepted by them, but it suggests that Wycliffe was trying to keep them from getting involved in the search.
Add this card to the victory display and remember that you "retrieved Wycliffe's letter."
Victory 2.

back.name: Best Laid Plans
back.text:
Finally, the fog of deception surrounding the expedition is beginning to lift. With the evidence you've gathered, you make your departure from the manor, sparing one final moment of silence for the murdered financier.

front.flavor_text: The assassins are still somewhere in the manor, but just who are they?  They seem to be the same group that robbed the O'Bannions, but if they're not working for Wycliffe, then for whom?  Whatever secrets Wycliffe knew, they clearly don't want to be discovered by others, which makes your mission that much more important now.

back.name: The Professionals
back.text:
Footsteps sound from the front of the manor as a trio of dark suited men enter. They say nothing, but observe for a moment before unpacking weapons and other tools from a briefcase. The other agents within the manor all give them a wide berth with a clear deference of rank as the three men set to work.
Spawn the set-aside Tick Tock Men at Entry Hall. Shuffle the encounter discard pile back into the encounter deck.

front.flavor_text: The assassins are still somewhere in the manor, but just who are they?  They seem to be the same group that robbed the O'Bannions, but if they're not working for Wycliffe, then for whom?  Whatever secrets Wycliffe knew, they clearly don't want to be discovered by others, which makes your mission that much more important now.

back.name: Cleaning House
back.text:
All at once, a great commotion sounds from the front of the house. Men in dark suits file inside with weapons drawn and other tools at hand. They spread throughout the manor with driven purpose, working to erase everything you're working toward. Your interference has become a priority problem to these men.
Put the set-aside Tick Tock Men into play next to the agenda deck. Shuffle the encounter discard pile back into the encounter deck.

front.flavor_text: These additional agents have sped up your schedule considerably.  If you don't deal with them, and soon, then they'll quickly erase everything you've worked to discover - if not you yourself.

back.name: Never Happened
back.text:
For the first time all night, through all the commotion and violence, you hear a brief silence. And then, a door slams shut. Footsteps grow louder toward you. Another door slams, and more footsteps join the first. Louder and closer, more footsteps and more slamming doors. You flee the mansion just ahead of a hail of bullets that stream after you, one of them striking your shoulder in the escape.
Each undefeated investigator who has not resigned is defeated and takes a physical trauma.

front.flavor_text:
An older man with a powerful frame stands just inside the entrance to the temple, glaring at you suspiciously.
He holds a sword in front of him in a ceremonial fashion, but he looks like he wouldn't hesitate to use it.  One way or another, you won't gain entry to the temple without dealing with him first.

back.name: Into the Grand Lodge
back.text:
If Luther Lynch is in the victory display:
With the situation as urgent as it is, you decide that it isn't worth trying to explain yourself. The man could be a cultist, for all you know, and is preventing your passage. After a brief struggle, you render him unconscious and proceed further into temple.
Shuffle the set-aside Cult of Cthulhuencounter set into the encounter deck. If the investigators parleyed with Luther Lynch:
Something about the imposing man strikes you as being more principled than the assailants you've encountered. You show the man that you mean to help the masonic order and quickly explain some of the threats that you seek to prevent. He looks back to the temple interior in thought before he slowly nods and stands to let you pass. "It is my duty to defend the grand lodge from those who seek to do it harm," he finally utters, "and though you are uninitiated, you will help me perform this duty if I allow you to pass."
Disengage Luther Lynch and flip him to his story asset side. Shuffle the set-aside Cult of Cthulhuencounter set into the encounter deck.

back.name: One Down
back.text:
If the act advanced because a Traitorenemy was defeated:
The man collapses down, but one last expression of accomplishment lingers on his face before he expires. These traitors are fanatically devoted to their cause to the point where death means nothing to them. Worse yet, the temple is still rife with saboteurs, which can only mean that there is at least one more traitor commanding them.
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Killed," record the name of the enemy that was defeated. Remove the corresponding story card from the game. Otherwise:
Your target suddenly cuts and runs, surprisingly nimbly for his age, and disappears around a corner. You attempt to pursue, but you find nothing but an empty hallway as you round the same corner. Despite his disappearance, his agents continue their attacks on you, which must mean there is at least one more traitor still within the grand lodge giving them directions.
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Alive," record the name of the enemy that left play.

back.name: Second Strike
back.text:
If the act advanced because a Traitorenemy was defeated:
The second traitor falls back with a gurgle, twitching and attempting to summon his strength for one final struggle, but failing. The infiltrators continue to stalk the halls in the silence after his death, which means there is yet another commander to quash.
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Killed," record the name of the enemy that was defeated. Remove the corresponding story card from the game. Otherwise:
You can't pin the second traitor down in time before he disappears in what can only be described as a crack in space. The cultist followers still rally inside the temple, which can only mean that there is another rat to sniff out.
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Alive," record the name of the enemy that left play.

front.flavor_text: Just how many of the Freemason elite have been chipping away at its foundations the whole time?

back.name: Rule of Three
back.text:
If the act advanced because a Traitorenemy was defeated:
With a final blow, the third traitor falls slain, and a stark silence washes over the grand lodge. Without leadership remaining at the temple, the cult agents have no doubt moved on to other pursuits, which leaves you to figure out just what those pursuits may be.
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Killed," record the name of the enemy that was defeated. Remove the corresponding story card from the game. (R3) Otherwise:
The third traitor vanishes, disappearing between ripples of air. Their mastery of the spatial warping power have proved to be an infuriating obstacle, though you find yourself standing in silent halls. The cult has retreated, but where to and for what purpose?
In your Campaign Log under "Cultists Alive," record the name of the enemy that left play. (R3)

front.flavor_text: Even knowing the evil that lurks within the grand lodge, there is a foreboding atmosphere the moment you approach the doors.  Something more arcane than hitmen and cover-ups is lurking inside.

back.name: Spatial Stirring
back.text:
If there are 3 cards in the Traitor Deck:
A vibration ripples through the air, not physically harming you but changing the atmosphere ever so slightly. Without your interference, this will likely be the mere beginning of something far worse.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. While it is next to the agenda deck, it gains " When an investigator would discard any number of cards from his or her deck: That investigator discards 1 additional card." Otherwise:
With the exposures already beginning, the remaining traitors are keeping their intentions masked. If you weren't considered a threat before, you certainly are now.

front.text: <for> When a <t>Traitor</t>enemy would leave play without being defeated: Move all doom on that enemy to the current agenda.
front.flavor_text: Even though a war is commencing in the very halls of the grand lodge, the Freemasons are still uncooperative and suspicious of you.  Is it because of their adherence to tradition, or are they attempting to hide their own betrayals?

back.name: Profane Prayers
back.text:
If there are 2 or more cards in the Traitor Deck:
Whispers part the still air of the temple. They are not uttered in any language devised by human minds, and send goose-bumps over your skin at the very sound of their syllables. Now you begin to see the deeper source of this madness.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. While it is next to the agenda deck, it gains " When an investigator would discard any number of cards from his or her hand: That investigator discards 1 additional card." Otherwise:
With more of the officers unmasked as infiltrators, you have inspired hesitation in the enemy. Whatever immortal force they serve, they are still mortal servants, and their dark work cannot be completed if you dispatch them all here and now.

front.text: <for> When a <t>Traitor</t>enemy would leave play without being defeated: Move all doom on that enemy to the current agenda.
front.flavor_text: While many of the infiltrators attack you outright, the important members are finishing their preparations to evade you.  If you don't finish unmasking these traitors soon, they will escape and leave little for you to trace them.

back.name: Back into Obscurity
back.text:
Another force wracks your brain, like an echo of the first ripple but much stronger, and you feel your psyche being stretched and sheared. You endure the pain for minutes on end until finally you collapse, utterly bewildered. This must have been the final effort from the traitors to incapacitate you and give themselves a further advantage. Unfortunately, it worked.
Each investigator who has not resigned is defeated and suffers a mental trauma.

front.subtitle: Manifold Measures
front.text:
<reaction> When <name> enters the play, choose one: Hand, Arcane, Accessory.  You gain 1 additional slot of the chosen type.
<reaction> When you play an asset that fills a slot of the chosen type, exhaust <name>: You get +1 to each of your skills until the end of the round.
front.flavor_text: Square your actions by the square of virtue with all mankind.

front.text:
Glen Conroy pulls a jeweled knife from inside his blazer and raises it threateningly as he backs away. Amid the standoff, he barks to his nearby minions to retrieve hidden caches of valuable weapons and artifacts scattered around the building. His preparations will be a problem.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Glen Conroy and this card from the game.

back.name: Glen Conroy
back.subtitle: Grand Treasurer
back.text: Investigators at Glen Conroy's location cannot gain more than 1 resource during the investigator phase.
back.flavor_text: The grand treasurer keeps a close watch on all financial and logistical matters within the lodge.  These resources could be dangerous if turned against you.

front.text:
Hector Sutton's eyes scan around you, as if focusing on something that did not exist in this reality. He cracks his cane on a nearby pillar and the world seems to fold together at that point, shortening space. Your brain rejects what it sees, but the man is ready to slow you down personally.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Hector Sutton and this card from the game.

back.name: Hector Sutton
back.subtitle: Deputy Grand Master
back.text: The maximum hand size of investigators at Hector Sutton's location is reduced by 2.
back.flavor_text: The deputy grand master is a man of action and ambition, but also an intellectual.  These qualities could make him a very dangerous potential foe.

front.text:
Paul Kellerman slinks back to the edges of the room, signalling his subordinates within the building. The obstacles and attacks against you will be harder to avoid as long as he remains to coordinate them.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Paul Kellerman and this card from the game.

back.name: Paul Kellerman
back.subtitle: Grand Secretary
back.text: Investigators at Paul Kellerman's location cannot draw more than 1 card during the investigator phase.
back.flavor_text: It is a simple matter for the grand secretary of the lodge to control the flow of information.  Is this a habit of professional secrecy or action against you?

front.text:
Rodney Duvall's posture loosens, but his sharp eyes stay fixed upon you, a glint of malice beginning to rise behind them. His slight smile remains, but he says nothing as he takes a handgun from his coat pocket. He is ready -- eager even -- to end this deception and resume his duty of wholesale murder.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Rodney Duvall and this card from the game.

back.name: Rodney Duvall
back.subtitle: Junior Grand Warden
back.text: Investigators cannot move from Rodney Duvall's location on the same turn that they entered it.
back.flavor_text: The junior grand warden is quietly observant, but has a talent for spotting you among the crowds.  Such scrutiny could be a major obstacle if he is indeed against you.

Ulysses Hill stands proudly as cult agitators around the building all call to him to lead them in prayer. The man obliges at once, shutting his eyes and mouthing foul words which you know in your heart to be profane. This fanaticism fuels your enemies and drives them to horrors you can only guess at.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Ulysses Hill and this card from the game.

back.flavor_text:
The grand master is the center of attention in all lodge matters, whether ceremonial, clerical, or otherwise.
Gravitas like this could be an obstacle if he is a traitor.

front.text:
Wallace Thorpe utters unearthly syllables and a faint blue glow begins to emanate around him. The man regards you cautiously, gauging whether or not you will make the first move or if he will, still a patient foe after being unmasked.
Move this card next to the agenda deck. At the end of the round, place 1 resource on this card from the token bank. If there are 2 resources on this card, remove Wallace Thorpe and this card from the game.

back.flavor_text: Few men in the grand lodge are as somber and tight-lipped as the senior grand warden.  Is he a recluse by nature or a bearer of forbidden knowledge?

front.flavor_text: Each new port is a new culture shock.

front.text: <action> Spend 1-3 resources: Search the top X cards of your deck for an <t>Item</t>asset and draw it, where X is 3 times the number of resources spent.
front.flavor_text: Your ship is slated to depart soon, but you may still have time to make some extra preparations at Kingsport's shops.

back.flavor_text:
You step off the train into Kingsport's city center.
The smell of the salt sea air fills you with both hope and fear.

front.text: <free> Choose and discard a card from your hand: Reduce <name>'s shroud by 2 for the next investigate action taken on it (to a minimum of 1).
front.flavor_text: While fickle and flighty, many of the artists have been affected by strange dreams of impossible landscapes, and could share some insights if you can spare the time.

back.flavor_text: Kingsport's southern seafront is the home to many landmarks, including an artists' colony.

front.text: <for> After you place a resource token on <name>, if there are any amount of clues on this location: Draw the top card of the encounter deck.
front.flavor_text: Since its abandonment as part of the defenses, the fortress has simply been a historical curiosity.  The local police would be less likely to suspect anything sinister at work here.

back.flavor_text: The first fortress from the earliest days of Spanish colonization, the stone fort was actively used in defense of the city almost to the turn of the century.

front.text: Resource tokens cannot be placed on <name> while there are any amount of clues on it.
front.flavor_text: The people at the cathedral keep quietly to themselves, making it a chore to thoroughly question everyone.

back.flavor_text: The basilica is also known as the Catedral de Las Palmas and the Catedral de Santa Ana.  It is a well-known landmark on the islands, and its plaza is a common meeting place.

front.text: <reaction> After an enemy spawns at or moves to <name>: That enemy gains aloof until the end of the round.  (Group limit once per round).
front.flavor_text: Despite the weather, crowds of people still flock to the beach, making it an easy possible hiding place.

back.flavor_text: Playa de Las Canteras is the most popular beach on Gran Canaria, boasting a natural coral sandbar that shelters the bay from the more dangerous waves and currents.

front.text: <action> Spend 5 resources, plus 2 resources for each clue on <name>: Place a resource token on <name> from the token bank. (Group limit once per game.)
front.flavor_text: While not as important a fixture as it used to be, the castle is still an administrative hub where you might find assistance.

back.flavor_text: The castle is one of Cape Town's oldest standing structures, having served many functions from fortress to town center to military prison.

front.text: <action>: Test <willpower> or <intellect> (3).  This test gets +1 difficulty for each clue on <name>.  If you succeed, place a resource token on <name> from the token bank.  (Group limit once per game.)
front.flavor_text:
The German firm Adolf Bleichert & Co. is developing a cableway system to more easily scale the mountain.
You might be able to convince their engineers to help you.

back.flavor_text: The largest and most iconic of the mountains surrounding Cape Town.  Table Mountain is a popular tourist attraction, recently having undergone construction for accessibility.

front.text: <action> Choose and discard 2 cards from your hand, plus 2 cards for each clue on <name>: Place a resource token on <name> from the token bank.  (Group limit once per game.)
front.flavor_text: The university is home to some of South Africa's most talented engineers, some of which may be willing to help fix the ship's engines.

back.flavor_text: The institution was founded almost a hundred years ago as a simple tertiary school, but the financial boom of South Africa's mining industry helped it grow to a full university.

front.text: Investigators at <name> must choose two options instead of one while resolving the forced effect on the Framed for Murder! story card.
front.flavor_text:
Unsurprisingly, the city's center of bureaucracy
does not take kindly to fugitives.

back.flavor_text: Originally designed as a secondary palace for the Sultan of Zanzibar, the building was later converted into offices for members of the British government who enforced the city's protectorate status.

front.text: <action> <action>: Heal 2 damage or 2 horror (or any combination thereof). (Limit once per game.)
front.flavor_text:
The dispensary provides medications of all variety,
but only to upstanding citizens of course.

back.flavor_text: The dispensary is a well-known landmark of Stone Town, constructed with elements of Zanzibari, Indian, and European design to embody the city's multicultural heritage.

front.text: <for> After you discover 2 or more clues from <name> during your turn: Ready and move an enemy in play once toward you. (Limit once per turn.)
front.flavor_text:
The fort may be a public building, but there are plenty of places where your enemies could be waiting to ambush you,
if you pry too much.

back.flavor_text:
The oldest building in Stone Town, also known as the
Arab Fort due to its construction by the Sultanate of Oman.
It has served many functions in the city's history, most recently as a railway terminal.

front.text:
Investigators at <name> cannot spend clues.
As an additional cost to investigate <name>, either spend 1 additional action or pay 2 resources (choose one).
front.flavor_text:
There are plenty of restrictions for visitors to
the Sultan's palace, wanted or otherwise.

back.flavor_text:
The residence of Khalifa bin Harub, Sultan of Zanzibar.
As the reigning power of Zanzibar, his palace is the center of administration for the city.

front.text: <for> After you discover a total 2 or more clues from <name> during your turn: Draw the top card of the encounter deck.  (Limit once per turn.)
front.flavor_text: The verdant gardens provide better cover for your enemies than for you, unfortunately.

back.flavor_text: The lush garden provides a pleasant atmosphere with some shelter from the Mediterranean sun.  It was originally intended for use by off-duty troops, but is open to the public.

front.text:
<for> After you discover any amount of clues from <name>: Take 1 damage.
<action>: Test <combat> or <agility> (3).  If you succeed, ignore the above forced ability until the end of the round.
front.flavor_text: Near the point, the British navy has a small stockpile of German sea mines left over from the Great War that they've been using for technical training.

back.flavor_text: The southernmost point of Gibraltar holds the famed rock of Gibraltar, as well as its lighthouse.  The mountainous shoreline of Morocco is visible across the straits.

front.text: Clues cannot be discovered from <name> while there are any number of enemies at <name>.
front.flavor_text: The fortifications hold many secrets, but just as many opportunities for ambushers to waylay you.

back.flavor_text: The dominant structure of Gibraltar is the tower of the old fortress known as the Moorish Castle.  It was first constructed by the Berber Empire centuries ago, and has stood through several major wars.

back.flavor_text: This district houses much of the city's native population.  Though originally separate from the European Quarter, the recent constructions on the east bank have helped unite the districts of Port Said into a surprisingly diverse community.

back.flavor_text: The lighthouse is one of the harbor's most famous landmarks, making it an easy meeting place.  Famously, the tower is the first structure in the world ever built from reinforced concrete.

back.flavor_text: Between the native Egyptian authorities, French developers, and the control of British and former Ottoman governments, the offices of the Suez Canal Company have always been a center of great attention within the port.

front.flavor_text:
All kinds of favors can be bought for those
who can find the right people.

back.flavor_text:
This triumphal arch was constructed by British architects, only recently finished after a decade of construction.
Its position close to the harbor makes it a frequent gathering place for vendors and tradespeople of all kinds.

front.text: <reaction> After an enemy enters <name>: Exhaust that enemy.  (Group limit once per round.)
front.flavor_text:
The old fortifications provide plenty of hiding places and
side routes to evade your pursuers.

back.flavor_text: The Sewri Fort is a series of elongated blockhouses and walls that were used in the city's defense over two hundred years ago.  The compound was transformed into a prison after modern defenses made it obsolete, and further converted into warehouses after that.

front.text: <free> If there are no clues on <name>: You feel as if your prayers have been answered.  Deal 2<investigator> damage to an enemy in play.  (Group limit once per game.)
front.flavor_text: The most frequent prayer to Ganesha is to remove obstacles keeping you from victory, and you could certainly use that.

back.flavor_text: A temple devoted to the Hindu god Ganesha some hundred years ago.  Those who seek the elephant-headed god's blessings of wisdom and success frequently visit with prayers.

front.flavor_text: The trainyards give you opportunities to injure your enemies or send them off on the wrong train.

back.flavor_text: The central railway station of Bombay, built to accommodate the city's increasing value as a trading port.  More people traverse this station than perhaps any other station in India.

back.flavor_text:
Another military fort, this one south out of the town and much more geared toward the training of troops
for combat in a tropical climate.

front.flavor_text: If you can convince the fort's commanders of a vague threat near the canals, then the ambushers might be effectively pinned down.

back.flavor_text: One of several U.S. army bases lining the Panama Canal.  The fort is an artillery battery first and foremost, though it has some degree of control over the canal operations.

front.text:

front.flavor_text: Between the horrid creatures lurking in the canal's waters, the agents hidden among the buildings, and the cultists lurking off in the nearby jungle, a guerrilla army awaits you.

back.flavor_text: The canal, famously constructed at the turn of the century, allows ships to pass between the Pacific and Atlantic without traveling around South America.  The Gatun Locks are the northernmost set of water locks that make the trip possible.

front.flavor_text:
If nothing else, the cathedral offers a little sanctuary
in the fight against your assailants.

back.flavor_text:
The cathedral is a relatively new fixture to the city,
but has already become a sanctuary to the masses.

front.flavor_text: The broad grounds give you plenty of space to outrun any enemies that may think to corner you here.

back.flavor_text: These lush botanical gardens were built on the grounds of the original town of Suva after its destruction by rival natives.  Recent renovations including the clock tower, bandstand, and drainage pipes have made it quite popular.

back.flavor_text: The library is one of the city's most prominent landmarks, and is a hallmark of the city as the cultural center of the immediate Pacific region.

back.flavor_text:
The sturdy stone buildings have served a surprising variety of functions over the past hundred years, including as a prison compound, hospital, immigration depot,
orphanage, legal court, and gold mint.

The proprietors here are always looking to make a profit,
and one of them just might have seen something suspicious.

front.flavor_text: With the vast knowledge stored at the garden, it's quite possible that one of the people responsible for amplifying the nightmares is hidden nearby.

back.flavor_text: Sydney's botanical garden functions not only as a public park, but as a highly respected institute for botanic research.  The herbarium and library attract the attentions of international scholars.

front.flavor_text: With the free flow of information at the terminal, you may be able to piece together the snatches of gossip into something concrete.

back.flavor_text: Also called Central Station, the building serves as a hub for travel through much of Sydney.  Trains, trams, taxis, and all other kinds of traffic converge here.

"Every ship is a romantic object, except that we sail in. Embark, and the romance quits our vessel,
and hangs on every other sail in the horizon."
<right>-- Ralph Waldo Emerson

back.flavor_text: Kingsport manages a surprising amount of international shipping for a harbor of its size, rivaling even nearby Boston.

front.flavor_text: Your ship to the Canary Islands will depart soon, you just have to get to Kingsport harbor to board it.

front.flavor_text: For a while, it seems as though your stay in South Africa will go without incident, but mere hours before departure, an explosion sounds within the ship's boiler rooms.  Your heart sinks as another hurdle places itself in your path.

back.name: Cape Town to Zanzibar
back.text:
You keep a vigilant watch at the harbor while the repairs are made to ensure that no further bombs are planted. This culprit was more careful than the last, as you find no sign of them by the time the engines are fixed. The captain orders immediate departure to not give the bomber another window to act.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Remove all doom from the current agenda. For each enemy in play, you must (choose one): That enemy stays in play. Move that enemy to Harborside if it is not already at Harborside. Discard that enemy and place 1 doom on the current agenda. Remove each other Cape Townlocation from the game. Put each of the set-aside Zanzibarlocations into play. (Location placement on page 20 in the Campaign Guide.) Put the set-aside Framed for Murder! story card into play next to the act deck.

front.text: At the end of the round, if "you have solved the Port Said problem," investigators at Harborside may choose to advance. (Warning: Each investigator not at Harborside will be defeated!)
front.flavor_text: You find smooth sailing once again until you make port in Egypt at the northern end of the Suez Canal.  The local port authority has completely shut down the canal for the foreseeable future.

back.name: Port Said to Bombay
back.text:
With the harbormaster's family rescued, he reopens the Suez Canal quickly and quietly. You return to the liner to prepare yourself for whatever trials and tribulations await in India.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Remove all doom from the current agenda. For each enemy in play, you must (choose one): That enemy stays in play. Move that enemy to Harborside if it is not already at Harborside. Discard that enemy and place 1 doom on the current agenda. Each investigator at a Port Saidlocation is defeated and takes 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice). Move each Port Said location with no clues on it and Victory X to the victory display. Remove each other Port Saidlocation from the game. Put each of the set-aside Bombaylocations into play. (Location placement on page 22 in the Campaign Guide.) Put the set-aside Assassins Close In! story card into play next to the act deck.

front.text: At the end of the round, if "you have solved the Suva problem," investigators at Harborside may choose to advance. (Warning: Each investigator not at Harborside will be defeated!)
front.flavor_text: Traveling across the Pacific compounds your feelings of unease.  From what little you know about Cthulhu, he dwells somewhere within the south Pacific, bringing you closer to his domain on this route than any other.

back.name: Suva to Sydney
back.text:
The seemingly-endless horde of monstrous fish creatures finally subsides, leaving the island quiet once again, but for the sounds of storm and sea. You shudder to imagine how many such creatures still lurk in the Pacific, but you are free to continue on your journey for now.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Remove all doom from the current agenda. For each enemy in play, you must (choose one): That enemy stays in play. Move that enemy to Harborside if it is not already at Harborside. Discard that enemy and place 1 doom on the current agenda. Each investigator at a Suvalocation is defeated and takes 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice). Move each Suvalocation with no clues on it and Victory X to the victory display. Remove each other Suvalocation from the game. Put each of the set-aside Sydneylocations into play. (Location placement on page 23 in the Campaign Guide.) Put the set-aside Feverish Dreams! story card into play next to the act deck.

front.text: At the end of the round, if "you have solved the Zanzibar problem," investigators at Harborside may choose to advance. (Warning: Each investigator not at Harborside will be defeated!)
front.flavor_text: A sense of unease follows you for the whole voyage to the British territory of Tanganyika.  As the ship begins to make port, a terrible scream cries out from just outside your cabin door.

back.name: Zanzibar to Singapore
back.text:
With the defeat of the actual murderer, you are able to explain to the police just what occurred. Thankfully, they accept your explanation without any complaint and grant you permission to board the next ship to Singapore.
Each investigator at a Zanzibarlocation is defeated and takes 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice). (R2)

front.text: At the end of the round, if "you have solved the Bombay problem," investigators at Harborside may choose to advance. (Warning: Each investigator not at Harborside will be defeated!)
front.flavor_text: You disembark at Bombay's docks, wary after the first two stops.  As expected, you spot shadowy figures lurking at the edges of crowds and down adjoining alleyways, watching your every move, though in greater number than before.

back.name: Bombay to Singapore
back.text:
The assassins bear down on you time and again, but you beat them back each time, until finally the survivors retreat into the dense backstreets of Bombay. You catch your breath and make for the harbor immediately, hoping the ship is ready to set sail.
Each investigator at a Bombaylocation is defeated and takes 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice). (R2)

front.text: At the end of the round, if "you have solved the Sydney problem," investigators at Harborside may choose to advance. (Warning: Each investigator not at Harborside will be defeated!)
front.flavor_text: You have been haunted by visions and nightmares of Cthulhu and cyclopean ruins since your journey began, but the intensity of these dreams spiked tremendously on your first night in Sydney.

back.name: Sydney to Singapore
back.text:
Exhausted but relieved, you finally are able to rest again. The nightmares still lurk in your psyche, but they won't be enough to kill you outright. Not yet, anyway.
Each investigator at a Sydneylocation is defeated and takes 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice). (R2)

front.text: (Warning: If this agenda advances, the scenario will end!)
front.flavor_text: With the agents of Cthulhu haunting your steps and spread across the world, it won't be long before they're able to track you down and corner you.  If you want to reach Singapore, then you'll have to adapt and act quickly.

back.name: The Net Closes
back.text:
The sound of approaching footsteps fades in as you rush down a side street. From behind, beside, and even in front of you, men in dark suits advance from the shadows. You try to defend yourself, but with their numbers, the agents rapidly overwhelm you.
Each investigator is defeated and suffers 1 physical or 1 mental trauma (your choice).

front.text:
Cape Town.
The ship's engineers report that an improvised bomb of some kind destroyed the ship's main drive shaft. Unlike in Las Palmas, this is a problem that could take days, if not weeks to fix. With no other ships heading eastward for some time, you have to find a way to speed up the repairs. You must be careful, however. Whoever sabotaged the engine may still be tailing you.

Colón.
As you disembark at Colón's port, you catch a glimpse of something moving in the bay -- several of the repulsive fish creatures allied with the cultists. You freeze and scrutinize their movements as they glide upriver. Your arrival surprised the cult's agents here in Panama, but they must be preparing some treachery for you further up the locks.
Flip this card and move it to Gatun Locks.

back.text:
Massive.

front.text:
Gibraltar.
A few short hours after your liner makes port, a derelict tanker limps into Gibraltar's harbor, barely afloat for the holes in its side. It grinds to a halt on the rocks of the bay, making it impossible for large ships to pass by. You have no doubt in mind that this event was concocted by your enemies, but you can't wait idly for the authorities to clear the ship.
Spend 4 clues as a group: Flip this card and resolve the revelation effect on the other side as if the lead investigator had drawn this card from the encounter deck.

front.text:
Las Palmas.
You inspect the rations at the harbor and find that they have indeed been poisoned deliberately. The captain can acquire more supplies easily enough, but he refuses to buy them until the poisoner has been caught. You can't set sail without supplies, nor can you wait on the local police, so you'll have to track down the culprit yourself.

front.text:
Port Said.
You argue on the docks with the harbormaster, but he will not be swayed by any appeal or reasoning. You can tell, however, that he is tense and clammy, and he avoids looking you in the eyes as you speak. The man is in mortal fear of something, but what? Is he being forced to hold you here by the cultists?
If "you found the blackmailers' hideout," flip this card and move it to the active investigator's location.

Suva.
As your ship docks at Fiji, motion once again draws your attention to the water. Dark figures mass together further out in the ocean, preparing for a massive assault all at once. With nowhere to escape to, you'll have to prepare for their inevitable attack.
After the third doom is placed on the agenda, flip this card and move it to Harborside.

Sydney.
Something is amplifying your nightmares, to the point of seriously damaging your personal well-being. You may not survive to board the next ship if you can't find the cause behind these spikes of intense delusions.

Zanzibar.

Things do not look good for you. If you want to prove your innocence and continue on your journey, you'll have to evade the police and track the true culprit yourself.

front.flavor_text: The chapel is a place of guidance for the city's citizens, though your problems aren't exactly normal.

back.flavor_text: The complex of buildings was originally dedicated as a school, but has since grown to include the orphanage, refuge, and grand chapel that it is known for today.

front.flavor_text:
Whether the grand lodge of Singapore has been infiltrated or not,
they won't appreciate your snooping around without good reason.

back.flavor_text: The masonic brotherhood has arguably existed in Singapore longer than the city itself has.  Sir Stamford Raffles, who founded and designed much of the city on behalf of the British Empire, was a well-known Freemason.

front.flavor_text: The sprawling docks offer many opportunities to those quick or stealthy enough to safely find them.

back.flavor_text:
You've only just arrived,
but you have a feeling you won't be staying long.

front.flavor_text: The mosque's architects work with both old and new styles, and may be able to give you insight into how to counter the cult architects.

back.flavor_text: A new mosque designed to celebrate the centenary of the community's older, and much smaller mosque.  The main structure is still under construction, but the architects estimate that it should be completed by the end of next year.

front.flavor_text: Much of the barrier's energy seems to be flowing through the stone monument.  It may cost you, but you may also gain some insight into how to break the barrier through it.

back.flavor_text: A monument dedicated to the citizens of Singapore who lost their lives fighting for the British in the Great War.  The tall stone plinth is flanked on either side with memorial plaques listing the names of the dead.

front.flavor_text: Your position may seem ludicrous, but if you can prove that you are being hunted, the local government may be convinced to help you.

back.flavor_text: The Istana is both the residence and office of the governor of Singapore.  Its design is a combination of classic imperial British designs with the more open layout typical of native Malaysian structures.

front.flavor_text: Self-reflection is a surprisingly taxing task, but the temple offers plenty of support to those seeking to find peace.

back.flavor_text: One of the oldest temples in Singapore, originally dedicated to the Chinese goddess Mazu, though it includes shrines to Buddha, Confucius, and many other deities.

front.text: <obj> If there is 1 <tablet> token in the chaos bag, you must immediately advance.
front.flavor_text: The longer this dome delays you, the more time your enemies have to prepare their ultimate goal.  Your clear goal is to destroy the geometric barrier, but how?

back.name: First Flux
back.text: Applying the knowledge gleaned from your initial observations, you work out a basic understanding of how the barrier works. As you solidify your theories, the dome begins to wobble, its shape losing consistency. If the mere knowledge of these arcane mechanics is enough to counter the barrier, then there may be hope for you yet.

front.text: <obj> If there are 2 <tablet> tokens in the chaos bag, you must immediately advance.
front.flavor_text: The architects' spell seems to rely on using both the knowledge of the spatial warping magic and the will to shape it.  You must match their wits and will with your own.

back.name: Second Shatter
back.text: Your understanding of the second principle further weakens the shifting dome. Cracks and splinters begin to cross through the various shapes and patterns, forming lines where the barrier takes longer to morph. Once your knowledge is complete, you will be free.

front.text: <obj> If there are 3 <tablet> tokens in the chaos bag, you must immediately advance.
front.flavor_text: You must apply the final leap of logic before the cultists can close the barrier in around you.  All that remains is to complete your understanding.

back.name: Final Fracture
back.text:
Your final breakthrough proves to be a literal one, as your discovery of the dome's inner workings unravels it completely. The geometric shapes fold into each other, winking out of existence or dissolving into the stonework of Singapore's landmarks, and leaving you free to leave the city as you will.
(R2)

front.flavor_text: The angular dome shimmers and flickers with power, distorting even the vectors of light flowing through it.  Wherever the barrier intersects with the terrain, buildings bend and shift impossibly, though somehow the structures remain standing.

back.name: Architectured Obstacles
back.text:
Your efforts to break the barrier have not gone unnoticed. One of the renegade architects emerges from the shadows, shifting the spell to counter you more directly.
Spawn the set-aside Barrier Architect at the closest location to the lead investigator without an investigator. If there are 2 or 3 names listed under "Cultists Alive:"
Alongside the cultists maintaining the barrier, you spy a familiar face from the Grand Lodge in Philadelphia, who no doubt has revenge in mind from your earlier interference.
Choose a listed name at random. Search the collection for the Traitor enemy with that name and spawn it at the furthest location from all investigators. Otherwise:
Your earlier efforts deprived the cultists of several capable agents, driving the remaining renegades to a more desperate state of mind.
Attach the set-aside Maddening Designs to Barrier Architect.

front.flavor_text: As the cult geometers focus their power, a sudden sound like scraping glass rips through the air.  Sections of the barrier begin to fold inward on themselves, slipping from existence entirely and steadily shrinking the size of the dome.  Cornered as you are, you cannot afford to be caged even further.

back.name: Fragmentation
back.text:
The scraping and receding barrier seems to lock into place, and with a fantastic display, the shapes all reform, combining and splitting, bending in ways that defy the world you inhabit. The very sight puts a pressure on your mind that you can barely withstand.
In player order, each investigator tests (5). Each investigator that fails removes the top X cards of his or her deck from the game, where X is the amount he or she failed by. If an investigator reveals a or token during this test, he or she automatically succeeds instead.

front.flavor_text: The brief reordering ends, and the dome continues to close in at an even more rapid pace.  Can you shatter it before it closes in on you?

back.name: Approaching Zero
back.text:
The abstract dome rushes downward and inward, closing on you ever faster until the sides and top crash upon you. Your body seizes and your mind spasms from the unnatural sensation, for agonizing minutes until at last, darkness overtakes your vision.
Each investigator is defeated and suffers a mental trauma.

front.flavor_text: Sukiman grips the steering wheel and shouts at you to get on deck.  He'll keep you on course provided you can repel the cult agents and act as his spotter through the warped seascape.

back.name: Landfall
back.text:
Sukiman steadies his ship as you plow through the waves forward, past another intersection of space. Fragments of reality converge in front of you, bringing a towering volcano into view. An island this size couldn't have possibly just emerged from Krakatoa's natural activity, which can only mean that the architects are at work here.
Read Scenario Interlude: End of the Line in the Campaign Guide.

front.text:
<reaction> After an investigator is moved by the forced effect on Impossible Summit: Move up to 2 clues controlled by investigators to this act.
<obj> At the end of the round, if there are at least 4<investigator> clues on this act, advance.
front.flavor_text: Space is bent around the volcano, keeping you from effectively scaling it.  Only careful study of the phenomenon and the surrounding slopes will tell if there is a way to bypass the architects' safeguards.

back.name: Mounting Perils
back.text:
Through repeated movement around and through the peak, you are able to pinpoint smaller stone fixtures that maintain the warping field. You easily deface the stones, and a clear path up to the peak appears nearby. At the same time that the path appears, an ungodly gurgling roar thunders across the peak, and the sound of leathery wings echoes dully across the peak. Something unearthly is atop the volcano with the architects.
Reveal Impossible Summit. Spawn the set-aside Star Spawn of Cthulhu at Impossible Summit. If there are 1 or more names listed under "Cultists Alive:"
The traitorous officers gather at the top of the peak, directly overseeing the final construction of their non-Euclidean monoliths. You knew that there had to be a reckoning, and that time has finally come.
Search the collection for each Traitorenemy listed and spawn each at Impossible Summit. Otherwise:
With your clearer view of the peak, the stone structures at the top appear more unstable than you expected. Without the leadership and expertise of the masonic traitors, the project has proceeded haphazardly.
Put this card next to the agenda deck. Impossible Summit gains " At the end of the round, each investigator at Impossible Summit discards the top 3 cards of his or her deck."

front.flavor_text: The glow of emerging magma dots the disjointed horizon.  The cult's work has begun, and already Krakatoa's new volcanic islands are being thrust upward and about like popcorn kernels.  Your approach to the center of operations will be all the more hazardous now.

back.name: Random Deviation
back.text:
The atmosphere cracks and shifts, and you can feel multiple fragments of space shifting around you. Something is about to converge on you, but what? Volcanic heat? A gap in space? An enemy lying in wait? You can only trust your instincts and prepare for the first thing you expect.
In player order, name a trait out loud and discard the top card of the encounter deck. If the discarded card does not have the named trait, take 1 damage and 1 horror or remove the top 3 cards of your deck from the game (choose one). After each player has resolved this effect, shuffle the encounter discard pile back into the encounter deck.

front.flavor_text: You soldier on through the fractured and molten landscape, though a tension lingers in the air around you.  With all the shearing of reality, the building pressure in the caldera's volcanoes may be released without warning.

back.name: Molten Ejection
back.text:
An explosion rocks the air, and a wave of heat and ash sweeps across you. Scattered chunks of tephra fling across the sky, though their trajectories are disjointed by the overlapping space. It's a matter of chance whether you're in the path of any of the debris.
In player order, each investigator must decide (choose one): If Warped Idol is ready, exhaust it. If Immutable Sigil is ready, exhaust it. Lose 1 action. You cannot move this round. Reveal a random chaos token. If you reveal a , , , , , or token, take 2 damage or discard an asset you control (choose one).

front.flavor_text: Space around the Krakatoa caldera is being stretched further apart with each passing second.  The architects must be finishing their designs to transpose R'lyeh to the surface.  Is it already too late to stop it?

back.name: Rise of R'lyeh
back.text:
A wave of force rushes out from the volcanic peak, reordering the world around it. The air fragments like shattered glass and you feel yourself pulled in a dozen different directions at once, straining your mind and body with fantastic intensity.
Each investigator is defeated and suffers a physical or mental trauma (your choice).

front.flavor_text: To find and destroy the pillars holding R'lyeh at the surface, you will first have to explore the island to make sense of its impossible perspectives.

back.name: The Non-Euclidean Pillars
back.text:
After all that you have seen, you are surprised to find some method to the madness at hand. The perspectives make sense in highly specific circumstances, impossible to truly comprehend, but like advanced scientific theories still work in practice. Through much trial and error, you finally can make your way to the bases of these pillars.
Put each set-aside copy of Impossible Pillar into play in the following orientations (in order, until each Impossible Pillar is in play): Down, Right, Left, Up.

front.text: : Rotate your investigator mini-card 90 degrees clockwise or counter-clockwise. Any investigator may place 1 of their clues on their location to reduce this ability's cost by 1 action (to a ability instead). Each R'lyehlocation gains "Non-Euclidean -- Place 1 horror on this location." After you move to a location, if the orientation of your investigator-mini card matches that location: Take a move action. (Limit 3 times per turn.) When a story card enters the victory display, you must immediately advance.
front.flavor_text: These pillars -- made in imitation of the unknowable -- must be toppled.  Only once they lie in broken ruin can this unnatural place return to whence it came.

back.name: Spatial Collapse
back.text:
If there are 1 or more Impossible Pillars in play:
As the pillar crumbles and folds out of existence, space buckles and the island seems to turn on its end. You dig your fingers into the soapy rock and pray that you're still right side up when the distortion recedes.
Flip back to act 2a. Otherwise:
The final pillar cracks and dissolves into the fragmented atmosphere with a hollow echo. Air and water rush in and around from all sides in a complete reversal of the event that brought R'lyeh to the surface. The sky spins one direction and the ground in the opposite, but through it all you see the figure of Cthulhu reaching towards you in dark fury.
(R4)

front.flavor_text: You tread in the domain of the dead dreamer Cthulhu.  How long will it be until he awakens?  You have no recourse but to work quicker than you ever have before, and hope beyond hope.

back.name: Awoken From Death
back.text:
A grinding sound reverberates throughout the island, the deep but shrill scraping of stone against stone. Through the inconstant landscape rises a titanic figure, the only thing clearly visible on the island from any angle. Its arms and wings raise as its booming voice carries terror through the air with it. The lord of R'lyeh has awoken.
Spawn the set-aside Cthulhu next to the agenda deck. Place each of the set-aside copies of Inescapable Reach next to the agenda deck, facedown. Place 1 horror on agenda 2a.

front.flavor_text: The terrible squid-dragon bears down on you, but the warped terrain of R'lyeh makes it difficult to see just where and when it will strike at you.

back.text:
If there is fewer than 3 horror on this agenda:
The pursuit drags on, and each moment brings the creature's thundering stride and lumbering grasp closer.
Place 1 horror on this agenda. Flip back to agenda 2a. Otherwise:
As R'lyeh's angles swallow and shift everything that touch them, the island seems to open up around Cthulhu. It is lord here, and you are trespassers in its unearthly domain.
Advance to agenda 3a.

back.name: Insurmountable
back.text:
There is no escape now. Cthulhu's webbed claws sweep down, mauling you savagely and scoring your mind with its unearthly voice. This accursed island was once its tomb, but now it shall be yours.
(R1)

front.text:
The world around this pillar seems to be completely out of phase. Only when you strain your mind to its limit does the pillar overlap with the island.
Choose an investigator at this location to test + (4). This test gets +2 difficulty. An investigator at this location may exhaust Warped Idol or Immutable Sigil to give +2 skill value for this test. If this test failed:
You can feel your mind twisting as you attempt to attune yourself to the pillar, triggering intense agony in your brain.
Each investigator at this location takes 1 horror. The performing investigator takes 1 additional horror. Proceed to If this test succeeded. If this test succeeded:
You continue to focus your mind for several intense minutes, keeping fixated on the pillar long enough for you to approach it and dislodge an unstable fragment.
Discard each card attached to this location and move this card to the victory display. Move each investigator and enemy at this location to Ruins of R'lyeh.
Victory 1.

sections.markdown:
# Fondations Cyclopéennes ## Des Angles Impossibles et une Pierre Surnaturelle *« Plutôt que de décrire fidèlement chaque construction ou chaque édifice, il s’attardait sur les impressions générales suscitées par les angles prodigieux et les surfaces de pierre – des surfaces d’une telle démesure qu’aucune créature terrestre ne saurait les occuper, et recouvertes d’images et de hiéroglyphes aussi repoussants que sacrilèges. Le passage sur les angles m’intriguait par ailleurs, tant il me rappelait une remarque du jeune Wilcox au sujet de ses rêves. D’après lui, la géométrie du paysage onirique qui l’entourait était aberrante, non-euclidienne ; elle évoquait de manière odieuse d’autres dimensions et d’autres sphères d’existence. » -- H. P. Lovecraft, L'Appel de Cthulhu* *Fondations Cyclopéennes* est une campagne en 8 parties pour *Horreur à Arkham : le Jeu de Cartes*, pour 1 à 4 joueurs. Cette campagne s'inspire de la nouvelle *L'Appel de Cthulhu* de H. P. Lovecraft ainsi que de faits réels, de folklore conspirationniste, et plusieurs autres éléments emblématiques d'Arkham.

## Règles Supplémentaires et Clarifications

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Remarqué

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Certains interludes et conclusions de la campagne *Fondations Cyclopéennes* demandent aux joueurs d'ajouter ou d'effacer des traits sous la mention « Remarqué » dans leur Carnet de Campagne. Pour ce faire, utilisez l'emplacement dédié sur la deuxième page du Carnet de Campagne.

Plus tard dans la campagne, des scénarios peuvent être modifiés en fonction du nombre de traits sous la mention « Remarqué » détenues par les investigateurs. Ces traits sont partagés entre tous les investigateurs, et non pas liés à l'un d'entre eux en particulier. La mention « Remarqué » n'a aucun effet sur la partie, sauf lorsqu'il y est explicitement fait référence par le Guide de Campagne ou le texte d'une carte.</family></size>

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Non-Euclidien

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>**Non-Euclidien** est une nouvelle capacité qui apparaît sur certains lieux. Chaque fois qu'un investigateur veut quitter un lieu, cet investigateur doit résoudre toutes les capacités **Non-Euclidien** de ce lieu.

Un lieu est « Non-Euclidien » pour le besoin d'autres effets de carte s'il a au moins une capacité **Non-Euclidien** (imprimée ou autre).</family></size>

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Alerte

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Chaque fois qu’un investigateur échoue à un test de compétence lorsqu’il tente d’échapper à un ennemi avec le mot-clé Alerte, après avoir appliqué tous les résultats du test de compétence, cet ennemi effectue une attaque contre l’investigateur ayant tenté de s’échapper. Un ennemi ne s’incline pas après avoir effectué une attaque consécutive au mot-clé Alerte. Cette attaque a lieu que l’ennemi soit engagé ou non avec l’investigateur qui tente de lui échapper.</family></size>

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Sceller

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Certaines cartes peuvent avoir la capacité de sceller un ou plusieurs pions Chaos dans le cadre de leur effet. Pour ce faire, procédez comme suit : allez chercher dans la réserve du Chaos le pion indiqué et placez-le sur la carte. Si le pion indiqué n'est pas dans la réserve du Chaos, l'effet échoue.

Quand un pion Chaos est « libéré », il retourne dans la réserve du Chaos et n'est plus considéré comme étant Scellé. **Si une carte avec un ou plusieurs pions Chaos Scellés sur elle quitte le jeu pour quelque raison que ce soit, alors tous les pions Chaos dessus sont immédiatement libérés.**</family></size>

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Test de Plusieurs Compétences

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Certains tests de compétences demandent à un investigateur de tester plusieurs compétences à la fois (exemple : « effectuez un test de </family><size 7><intellect><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>< >+< ></family><size7><combat><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>< >»). Un tel test est considéré comme étant un test de chacun des types de compétence indiquée. Des cartes portant l’une ou l’autre des icônes de compétence peuvent être attribuées à ce test, et les deux icônes sont considérées comme étant des icônes correspondantes.

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Cachée

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Certaines cartes Rencontre possèdent le mot-clé Cachée. Une carte Cachée a une capacité **Révélation** qui l’ajoute secrètement à votre main sans révéler cette carte ni son texte aux autres investigateurs. Tant qu’une carte Cachée est dans votre main, traitez-la comme si elle était dans votre zone de menace. Ses capacités permanentes sont actives et les capacités inscrites dessus peuvent être déclenchées, mais seulement par vous. Une carte Cachée compte dans la taille de votre main mais ne peut en être défaussée par aucun moyen, excepté celui inscrit sur la carte. Quand une carte Cachée est défaussée, elle est placée dans la pile de défausse Rencontre. Elle ne reste pas partie intégrante de votre deck comme les faiblesses. Pour profiter de la meilleure expérience de jeu possible, les joueurs sont encouragés à «< >jouer le jeu » et à ne rien partager des informations sur toute carte Cachée dans leur main.</family></size>

<family "Teutonic"><size 14.0>

### Patrouille

</family></size>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Certains ennemis possèdent le mot-clé Patrouille. Lors de la phase des Ennemis (à l'étape structurelle 3.2), chaque ennemi redressé et non-engagé ayant le mot-clé Patrouille se déplace vers un lieu connexe en direction du lieu désigné (entre parenthèses à côté du mot-clé Patrouille) par le chemin le plus court possible.</family></size>

## Icône d'Extension

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>Les cartes de la campagne *Fondations Cyclopéennes* peuvent être identifiées grâce à ce symbole, placé devant le numéro de collection de chaque carte.</family></size></justified>

## Prologue

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>*Samedi 12 novembre 1927. Arkham, Massachusetts.

Les nombreuses campagnes archéologiques de l'Université Miskatonic ont souvent captivé l'imagination du public, autant par les connaissances rapportées de ces contrées éloignées que par les curiosités qui y furent découvertes. Bien qu’elles ne fussent souvent qu’en nombre très limité, les antiquités trouvées étaient souvent exotiques et intéressantes à plus d'un titre. Depuis ces huit derniers mois, l'université a bénéficié de fonds généreux de la part d'un entrepreneur, James Wycliffe, en vue de financer de multiples missions autour du globe. Chaque expédition a été couronnée de succès, enrichissant aussi bien la réputation des participants que les collections du Musée Miskatonic.

Celle de Mycènes, en Grèce, était tant attendue que les professeurs les plus passionnés de l'université avaient décidé d’annuler leurs cours pour être présent lors de son arrivée à Arkham. Mais les cours ont finalement bien eu lieu… car l'expédition n’est pas rentrée ce jour-là.

Vous imaginiez que le retard eût pu être causé par le mauvais temps ou, pire, par un naufrage, mais ce à quoi vous ne vous attendiez pas, c'est à la lettre de James Wycliffe lui-même, qui vous était personnellement adressée. Vous n'avez vu aucun coursier arriver ou repartir, mais la missive vous attendait sur votre paillasson le lendemain à la première heure.*</family></size></justified>

<center><image "C:\Users\guillan\OneDrive - S.D.I.S. 26\Documents\Fondations Cyclopéennes VF\Guide de Campagne\lettre_de_wycliffe-removebg-preview.png" 3.5in>

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10><left>*La liste imprécise des objets disparus et la copieuse avance de fonds joints à la lettre n'ont fait qu'accroître vos soupçons. Pourquoi Wycliffe suspecte-t-il un acte criminel ? Pourquoi insiste-t-il pour qu'une mission aussi importante demeure confidentielle ? Et pourquoi s'adresser à vous en particulier ? Votre expérience en matière d'enquête vous amène généralement sur le terrain du paranormal. Si l'expédition de Wycliffe a permis de découvrir quelque chose de cette nature, qui pourrait l'avoir appris assez vite pour l'intercepter ? De nombreuses questions restent pour l'instant sans réponse, mais vous n'avez que peu de temps pour vous préparer à passer une soirée bien occupée.*</family></size></justified>

## Scénario I : Amarres Brisées

<justified><family "Arno Pro"><size 10>*Vous passez la majeure partie de la journée à vous préparer. Dès lors que vous êtes prêts à vous rendre sur les berges de la Miskatonic, la pluie commence à tomber sous un ciel gris de novembre, et le vent se renforce de plus en plus. Si la tempête qui approche continue à ce rythme, elle sera à son apogée lorsque vous serez sur place. Même s'il serait sage d'attendre que le temps s'améliore, chaque minute perdue diminue l'espoir de retrouver la cargaison égarée.

Resserrant votre manteau, vous marchez dans les rues d'Arkham, tout en repassant les informations fournies par Wycliffe. L'expédition de Mycènes est arrivée directement à Kingsport depuis la Grèce. Sa cargaison a été transbordée d'un paquebot à une barge. Cette barge a ensuite remonté la Miskatonic grâce à un remorqueur nommé Myra Louise. Ce même remorqueur, qui a acheminé les trouvailles de l'expédition précédente, navigue sur la Miskatonic depuis plus de vingt ans sans incident. Néanmoins, le Myra Louise n'a pas atteint Arkham la nuit dernière et reste introuvable depuis son départ de Kingsport.

La clé pour élucider la disparition de la cargaison, ainsi que pour répondre à vos propres interrogations sur la mission confiée par Wycliffe, réside dans la localisation du remorqueur évanoui. Vous quittez votre maison et vous vous dirigez vers la rivière, vous abritant des intempéries alors qu'une curiosité croissante vous assaille. Une atmosphère troublante règne sur Arkham ce soir, bien plus que l'habituelle ambiance empreinte de superstition. Certaines des personnes que vous croisez agissent comme des somnambules, à peine conscientes de leur environnement et marmonnant dans un discours décousu. D'autres vous dévisagent avec méfiance et crainte, détournant les yeux lorsque vous les observez. Et peut-être est-ce votre imagination, mais ne dirait-on pas des silhouettes sombres qui se déplacent dans la rivière ?*

<right> <family "Arno Pro">Continuez à la **Mise en Place**.</family></size>
